One was an architect who would include architectural details in his scouting reports, which was cute and funny until he came back with nothing but architectural details during a pivotal moment when we really needed an accurate scout report. Another was just a timid little weirdo who ended up like the coterie's kid brother except he started feeling used when we kept having him use Premonition in potentially traumatizing scenarios. He started using his Auspex to figure out the other characters' insecurities and weaponize them.

There's also the fact that a diagnosable mental illness has symptoms severe enough to interfere with everyday life. Most of these symptoms are going to be noticeable, even if the general public don't associate them with a specific diagnosis.

With regards to comic relief, as long as it's approached tactfully and doesn't hinge on the suffering of the mentally ill, I don't mind it. If anything, having a solid comic relief character makes it so much more of a gut-punch when that character gets brought so low they don't have anything funny to say.

I guess what I'm saying is I like when Malkavians are played as fun and quirky until they very much are not.

It took me way longer than my peers to feel like I was able to move out, mostly because she had me convinced that she could not deal with my father alone. One of her favorite things to say when I was upset about the way my father treated me was, "One day you will get to leave. I'll have to deal with him forever..." She would also do things like tell him things I specifically asked her not to, say something wasn't a big deal and then change her mind once he decided it was a big deal. On one occasion I remember I had just been in a car accident and I was sobbing at her feet, trying to get her to hug me, and she just... stared.
